one_sentence: The three metaphysical questions—why something, why intelligible, why it matters—are formal requirements that any complete system must satisfy, and the 7Q Universal Classifier proves exactly one worldview survives elimination.
executive_summary: This document argues that the three classic metaphysical questions—why there is something rather than nothing, why what exists is intelligible, and why anything matters—are not philosophical decorations but formal requirements specifications for any candidate system. A system that cannot answer all three is architecturally incomplete, a stronger condition than Gödel-incompleteness. The God Story thought experiment (you wake up as God, alone, good, infinite) serves as a requirements-extraction device, generating constraints that map directly onto axioms in the spine. The 7Q Universal Classifier operates in forward mode (classifying any worldview into a unique 7-tuple) and reverse mode (elimination funnel). Starting with 60 worldviews, Z3/CVC5 SMT solvers verified 46 of 47 eliminations, leaving one worldview: external source, personal reality, moral problem, grace solution, relational telos, falsifiable verification. This is not selection bias but a verified funnel. The conclusion: the God Story worldview is the only M-complete system.
short_summary: This document is the first page of the axiom chain, establishing the metaphysical requirements any complete system must satisfy. Its core structural claim is that the three questions (existence, intelligibility, meaning) are formal constraints, not preamble. Key evidence includes the 7Q Universal Classifier elimination funnel, with 46 of 47 eliminations verified by Z3/CVC5 SMT solvers, reducing 60 worldviews to one. This matters because it provides a checkable, formal foundation for the entire Theophysics framework, grounding theology in requirements engineering.
